FM stands for "Facility Management," and within the Group it is limited to businesses related to commercial facilities. The company and its consolidated subsidiary AP Renovations Co., Ltd. (100.0% voting rights held) handle it. Net sales for the fiscal year ended December 2025 were ¥14,578 million (down 0.6% from the previous fiscal year), and segment profit was ¥203 million (down 47.7%). The securities report states that renovation work requiring store operations to be suspended was postponed until the third quarter and concentrated in the fourth quarter, increasing costs such as urgent imports and delivery by charter flights, so profit did not increase even though sales increased.
entries.6f9216650d73302d: On November 15, 2000, Ripplewood Holdings LLC, a U.S. investment fund, solicited investors in Japan and established the predecessor AlphaPurchase Corporation (the former AlphaPurchase) as a trading company providing products and services centered on MRO (Maintenance Repair and Operations). The head office was placed in Uchisaiwaicho, Chiyoda Ward, Tokyo. In January 2001, it began business as a trading company providing MRO-related products and services to large companies.

entries.7d4cd507ac1176a0: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that the group (the company and 3 subsidiaries) provides customers with mechanisms and services for purchasing goods and services efficiently, appropriately and at low cost, centered on two main businesses, the MRO business and the FM business, and aims to realize customers' optimal purchasing. The MRO business sells indirect materials such as tools, consumables, repair parts and stationery, and the FM business provides support for the construction, renovation, repair and cleaning of commercial facilities and supplies building materials. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥58,922 million (up 5.3% from the prior fiscal year), of which the MRO business accounted for ¥44,321 million and the FM business for ¥14,578 million.
entries.807c64e575aaf89a: A reportable segment that efficiently delivers indirect materials, such as tools, consumables, repair parts and stationery that companies buy on a daily basis, from order to delivery through an internet procurement system; it is the reportable segment with the larger revenue from external customers of the two reportable segments. The company is responsible for this segment. MRO is an abbreviation of "Maintenance Repair and Operations." Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥44,321 million (up 7.5% year on year), and segment profit was ¥1,186 million (up 54.2% year on year). The securities report states that the increase in profit was due to the automatic replacement recommendation feature for purchased items introduced in the electronic catalog "Mugen Catalog," which concentrated customers' purchases on best-selling products and raised the gross profit margin. On the other hand, in the fourth quarter, the impact of the ransomware attack on ASKUL halted sales to small and medium-sized businesses through ASKUL, and the resumption of shipments was also delayed, causing revenue to fall below the prior year.
entries.88290b82525ea169: A company that sells indirect materials such as tools and stationery, and store maintenance and renovation, to large corporate groups through an online purchasing system.
entries.89326bbc4f11b476: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥58,922 million (up 5.3% from the prior fiscal year). The MRO business was ¥44,321 million (up 7.5%), the FM business was ¥14,578 million (down 0.6%), and Other was ¥21 million (down 66.6%). The annual securities report states that MRO business revenue fell below the prior year, as sales via ASKUL stopped in the fourth quarter due to the ransomware attack on ASKUL and the resumption of shipments was delayed. FM business revenue rebounded sharply as renovation work was concentrated in the fourth quarter, and for the full year was in line with the prior year.
